description: Experiment record (issue #157): a muravev-style restructuring (arXiv:2401.11029, optimization 5 — the same idea behind java_points_to_muravev2024.cnf and c_alias_muravev2024.cnf) of the uniprot (unigraph) CFPQ grammar. The in-archive unigraph_N.cnf grammars materialize a very dense intermediate matrix M_Seq ~= M_X union M_X.cf.M_X (X = IsSimilar) and perform dense x medium products, which makes FastMatrixCFPQ OOM on unigraph_9/10 and take 67 min - 4.8 h on unigraph_4-8. The transformed grammar below keeps the same language and terminal set but never uses a dense nonterminal as a standalone factor in a binary production: every multiplication of the dense IsSimilar matrix is terminal x dense or dense x terminal, and the top-level product Lp.N3 pairs two terminal-anchored (edge-count-bounded) matrices. No archive or package change ships with this record — it documents the transformation and its verification so the sparse grammar can be reused as a low-memory oracle for the large unigraph graphs.

equivalence.original_language: With X = IsSimilar, R = refers_to.refers_to_r, cf = codes_for: S = Seq.R.X with Seq = X | X.cf.X and X = eps | has.X.has_r | iso.X.iso_r.X | bt.X.bt_r | pi.X.pi_r. So L(S) = X.(eps|cf.X).R.X = R.X union X+.R.X union cf.X.R.X union X+.cf.X.R.X.
equivalence.transformed_language: S -> N3 | Lp.N3 with N3 = IsAssociated.IsSimilar (= R.X), Lp = St1|St2|St3|St4 | CfX | St1.CfX | St2.CfX | St3.CfX | St4.CfX, where St_i is one outermost X step (has/iso/bt/pi anchored) and CfX = cf.IsSimilar. So L(S) = R.X union (St1|St2|St3|St4).R.X union cf.X.R.X union (St1|St2|St3|St4).cf.X.R.X.
equivalence.why_equal: A non-eps X is exactly ONE outermost step (X+ = St1 union St2 union St3 union St4): the nested balanced (Dyck-like) structure of X is carried by the recursive IsSimilar productions, while each St_i contributes precisely its outermost pair of terminals. Substituting gives L(S) identical to the original language.
equivalence.pitfall: A flat 'run of steps' restructuring (Lp -> Step.Lp | ...) is NOT equivalent: X is nested, not a Kleene star. The flat prototype accepted 480556 pairs on unigraph_1 vs the correct 376578 — it over-approximates by allowing arbitrary concatenations of steps.
equivalence.sparsity: The dense M_Seq matrix is eliminated; every multiplication of dense IsSimilar is terminal x dense or dense x terminal, and Lp.N3 pairs two terminal-anchored (edge-count-bounded) matrices.

verification.method: For each graph, ONE streamed .g edge list (terminal sets are identical) is solved once per grammar — the original in-archive unigraph_N.cnf and unigraph_1_sparse.cnf; counts must be equal to each other and match the recorded references in temporal_cfpq/results/reference_answers.csv. Peak RSS of the solver process measured with /usr/bin/time -v inside the container.

differences.note: On the small verification graphs the sparse grammar is not faster (the dense intermediate is still affordable there) and uses slightly more peak RSS; its purpose is to avoid the OOM on unigraph_9/10 and cut the 67 min - 4.8 h runtimes of unigraph_4-8, where the original grammar's dense M_Seq does not fit.
